resources.string: VettID keeps your messages, connections and most important secrets in a vault that only you can open.
Your keys stay on this phone and in your vault\'s sealed enclave.
You need a VettID membership: the account site gives you a code to set up your vault here.
I lost my phone: recover my vault
On the account site (Vault, then Set up your vault), get a setup code and scan its QR code with this phone. It works once, for 5 minutes.
That is not a VettID setup code. Scan the QR code the account site shows under Set up your vault.
That is a recovery code. To recover your vault, go back and choose \"I lost my phone\".
That code is from another VettID environment (%1$s), not the one this app uses. Get a code from this app\'s account site.
That code did not work. It may be mistyped, used already, or older than 5 minutes, or the email may not be your account\'s. Get a new code on the account site.
Enter your account\'s email address and the 8 characters shown under the QR code on the account site.
Codes have 8 characters and never contain 0, 1, I, L or O.
You are setting up a vault for %1$s. Only continue if this is your own account and you got the code yourself.
Your account already has a vault
A vault has exactly one app, which holds its credential. Another phone is that app. Move VettID to this phone from there, or recover the vault if that phone is lost.
Move VettID with a direct transfer: the other phone shows a code, this phone scans it, and you approve there with your PIN and credential password. No waiting.

Start a recovery on the account site. After 24 hours it shows a code that this phone scans; then your PIN and credential password move the vault here, and the old phone erases VettID the next time it reaches your vault.
Set up a new vault anyway
Your PIN unlocks your vault. Only your vault\'s sealed enclave ever checks it, and wrong guesses are slowed down. Use at least 6 digits; avoid dates and simple patterns.
The PINs do not match. Try again.
It protects your Protean Credential and your critical items, and VettID asks for it at every critical action. Make it different from your PIN. Nobody, VettID included, can reset it.
Choose where your credential lives. You can change this later in Credential.
Your vault keeps a copy sealed to it and to your password. If you lose this phone, a recovery restores your vault on a new one.
Your credential lives only on this phone. No copy exists anywhere else.
If this phone is lost, broken, reset or replaced without a transfer, your vault cannot be recovered. It can only be deleted and replaced by a new one, and everything in it is lost.
I understand that without this phone my vault cannot be recovered
This takes a moment. Keep VettID open.
Verifying the vault service and this phone
Your vault is enrolled, this phone holds its credential, and only your PIN opens it.
Invite someone with a QR code or a link, compare the safety code, and start messaging. Connections arrive in the next update.
Your vault now runs release %1$d (fingerprint %2$s); this phone last used release %3$d. Another of your devices approved this update. Continue only if you expected it.
Your vault is served by release %1$d, older than release %2$d that this phone last used. VettID will not send your PIN to it.
It ends on %1$s. Update to keep your vault working.
Update to the newest release to keep your vault working.
Your vault runs release %1$d. Release %2$d (fingerprint %3$s) is available. Anyone can rebuild it and compare the fingerprint.
Approve the update with this unlock
Too many wrong PINs. Try again in %1$s.

Someone started a recovery of this vault from the account site, so it is locked for this phone. If that was you on a new phone, let it finish there. If it was not you, cancel it now: unlocking here with your PIN cancels the recovery.
Your vault\'s state is older than expected
The vault\'s stored state is older than state this phone has already seen. Someone may have restored an old copy. Contact VettID support before you continue.
The update was refused (%1$s). Your vault stayed on its current release.
This phone cannot unlock your vault yet: it was moved here while your vault ran an older release. It can unlock once your vault is updated.
Your vault did not recognise this phone. It may have been replaced by a recovery or a transfer.
Your vault did not recognise this phone
This phone may have been replaced by a recovery or a transfer while it was offline. If your vault now works on another phone, you can erase VettID from this one.
Your vault is refusing this phone
Messages from this phone to your vault keep being refused. If you moved VettID to another phone, this one may have been replaced. Enter your PIN to check with your vault.

This erases VettID\'s data on this phone only: its keys, your account details and the app\'s settings. Nothing else on the phone is touched, and it works without a connection.\n\nIt cannot be undone. If this phone still holds your vault, you will need a recovery on another phone to use it again.
Use your fingerprint, face or screen lock to open VettID.
Use your phone\'s PIN, pattern or password to open VettID.
Use your phone\'s PIN, pattern or password
Your vault is on this phone now
Your old phone no longer holds it, and the credential copy it held no longer works; it erases VettID the next time it reaches your vault. Your desktops and agents stay paired.
Your old phone erases VettID as soon as it hears from your vault. Unlock with the same PIN and credential password as before.
Your old phone erases VettID as soon as it hears from your vault. Your vault runs an older release, so this phone cannot unlock it after it locks until your vault is updated.
Your account site shows a recovery QR code 24 hours after you start a recovery there. Open it (Vault, then Recovery, then Show the code) and scan it with this phone.
The recovery code from the account site, your vault PIN and your credential password. This phone then replaces your old one, which erases VettID the next time it reaches your vault.
Point the camera at the code on the account site.
VettID uses the camera only to read the code; nothing is recorded.
That is not a VettID recovery code.
That code is from another VettID environment (%1$s), not the one this app uses.
That recovery code is from an older account site. Reload the recovery page on the account site and scan the new code.
This recovery is not available: its code may not be ready yet (24 hours after the request), or the recovery was cancelled, used or has expired. Check the account site.
Checking the code with your vault
That code is not right. After 5 wrong codes the recovery is cancelled. Wrong codes from this phone: %1$d of 5.
That was the fifth wrong code, so the recovery was cancelled. Start a new recovery on the account site.
This code has expired. Start a new recovery on the account site.
This code is not valid yet. Try again later.
This recovery is no longer active: it was cancelled, already used, or voided after wrong codes. Start a new recovery on the account site.
Your vault could not verify this phone (device attestation). The code is still valid; this phone may not be supported.
Your vault could not answer just now. Try again.
The code was accepted. Unlock your vault with your PIN. Wrong PINs are slowed down, as on your old phone.
The recovery was cancelled before this phone finished it. Start a new recovery on the account site.
Its credential backup was off, so VettID offers no way back into it: nothing in it can be released to a phone without the credential.
This vault cannot be recovered: its credential backup was off. Delete it on the account site and start over with a new setup code.
Delete my vault and start over
I have a new setup code
Your vault checks it against its copy of your credential and hands the credential to this phone. Your old phone\'s copy stops working.
Too many wrong passwords. Try again in %1$s.
Your vault has no credential, so it cannot be recovered. Contact VettID support.
On your old phone, open VettID, then Settings, then Move to a new phone. It shows a code: scan it with this phone.
You will approve the move on the old phone with your vault PIN and credential password. The old phone then erases VettID.
Point the camera at the code your old phone shows.
On the old phone, copy the code under the QR code and paste it here.
That is not a transfer code. On your old phone, open Settings, then Move to a new phone.
That code has expired. Show a new one on your old phone.
Your old phone shows a code too. If they are the same, approve the move there with your PIN and credential password.
Waiting for your old phone (%1$s left)
The move was rejected on your old phone. Nothing changed: your vault stays there. To try again, show a new code on the old phone.
It was not approved within 10 minutes. Nothing changed. Show a new code on your old phone to try again.
Your vault did not answer. The code may have been used already, or this phone could not be verified. Show a new code on your old phone.
Camera view for scanning the code
Release notes are information. What keeps your vault safe is the signed release list and the fingerprint below.
Approve release %1$d for your vault with your vault PIN.

VettID locks your vault, opens it again with your approval, and then opens it on the new release. This takes a moment; a release that has to start first can take a few minutes. Your vault stays locked meanwhile.
It has ended and is open only so that you can move your vault. Update now to keep it.
Your vault is waiting for its daily PIN and password check. Do the check first, then update.
Your vault is up to date
Your vault runs the newest release.
Release %1$d is starting. This can take a few minutes.
Keep VettID open until this is done.
Your vault now runs release %1$d (fingerprint %2$s) and is open.
Your vault stayed on release %1$d and is open.
Release %1$d is not an active release in the release list your vault trusts.
Release %1$d is not newer than your vault\'s release.
Your vault could not verify this phone\'s approval.
Your vault did not accept the sealing key of release %1$d.
Another update is already under way for your vault.
Your vault could not record the update. Try again later.
The update did not go through
Nothing changed: your vault stays on release %1$d and is open.
Nothing changed: your vault stays on release %1$d. It is locked; enter your PIN to try again.
Too many wrong PINs. Wait, then try again.
The new release did not start. Try again later.
Release %1$d did not open your vault
Your vault was moved to release %1$d but did not open there. Try again, or return to release %2$d: that is possible until release %1$d has opened your vault once.
Your vault was moved to release %1$d but did not open there. Try again with your PIN.
Your vault goes back to release %1$d and opens there. You can approve release %2$d again later.
Your vault runs release %1$d again and is open. You can update to release %2$d later.
